newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures climbed as weaker-than-expected U.S. economic data provided some reassurance for bond markets ahead of a two-day U.S. policy making committee meeting starting on Tuesday.

Traders said the rise in U.S. bonds late in the session after the data prompted some to cover short positions opened earlier in the day - including some hedging in Paris of the German 30-year Bund issue - sparking a squeeze into the close.
Analysts said despite further gains in the GLOBEX session, the contract reached a high of 129.60, a number of factors looked set to keep the market restrained.

Although the widely held market view was that the U.S. Federal Reserve would leave interest rates unchanged, there was still a certain amount of caution as more and more people were expecting a rate rise in the coming months.

A key U.S. jobs release due on Thursday and worries about budget negotiations in Germany, important for assessing whether a likely French 1997 deficit budget overshoot would be a problem, were also likely to cap gains, they said.
With little hard European news to go on some traders said the optimism in the French stock futures pits, the CAC 40 index hit a record on Tuesday, was spilling over to bond futures.
"I think the rally has been fueled by the strong performance of the CAC and some short covering from traders who sold this morning," the head of a French brokerage said.
"All (the franc bond) issues today were well absorbed... U.S. bonds are performing extremely well and the (U.S. NAPM) number was a shade better than people were expecting," he said.

Philippe Brossard, head of research at ABN Amro Finance, said, "People tended to hedge themselves on the French market before the German (30-year Bund) auction and there was some unwinding. NAPM was less than expected, although its still very strong, so fears (of a rate rise) have been pushed away."
"The numbers today were reassuring. By and large we fall into the into the no inflation, no need for a rate hike camp," Sonja Gibbs, bond analyst at Nomura International, said.

While many analysts remained cautious ahead of this week's events, one trader said the high levels of liquidity in the French market and the fact money was being put back into positions after being removed before the end of June could push the bond future past 130 by the end of the week.
The 30-year area of the French curve continued to outperform Germay with the yield spread moving to minus three basis points from parity on Tuesday and plus one on Friday.
French long-dated OATs also outperformed the rest of the curve after suffering slightly in recent days. The 10-year spread between French and German bonds was unchanged at minus 13 basis points.
Traders said French bonds were also being helped relative to Bunds as frustration with the lack of performance from spread narrowing trades was prompting some to buy back OATs.

The Treasury said it would be selling 21 to 23 billion francs of OATs, with nearly 20 billion in the new 5.50 percent October 25, 2007 OAT. The rest of the supply will be the 2009 TEC 10 OAT, said to be in demand from some domestic investors.
The Treasury will not be selling any Ecu OATs this month although it still has the option to sell Ecu BTANs in the third week of July at the time of the franc BTAN auction.

The French franc and September PIBOR were little changed. The franc was at 3.3703 per mark compared with 3.3695 late on Monday and it climbed from early lows against the dollar to 5.8720 late in the session.
